newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bank of Ikeda to write off Y24 bln problem loans.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Ikeda to write off Y24 bln problem loans.

text.p: Bank of Ikeda Ltd said on Tuesday that it plans to write off 24 billion yen worth of problem loans in the financial year ending on March 31.
The amount is higher than the initially planned write-off figure for the year of 15.9 billion yen, the bank said in a statement.
The medium-sized regional bank said it plans to earn 4.6 billion yen in profit from the sale of stock holdings in 1996/97 and 1.5 billion yen from the sale of its land holdings.

As a result of that and the write-offs, the bank said it would post a net loss of 13.5 billion yen for 1996/97, sharply revising down its earlier estimate of a net profit of 800 million yen for the year.
The bank also said it would eliminate bonus payments to its senior executives for 1996/97, and was also considering freezing its workers' base salaries for the year starting on April 1.
